source.author: ov
source.text: Diffugiunt populi nec se nisi moenibus urbis esse putant tutos, donec Meleagros et una lecta manus iuvenum coiere cupidine laudis: Tyndaridae gemini, spectatus caestibus alter, alter equo, primaeque ratis molitor Iason, et cum Pirithoo, felix concordia, Theseus; et duo Thestiadae prolesque Aphareia, Lynceus et velox Idas, et iam non femina Caeneus Leucippusque ferox iaculoque insignis Acastus Hippothousque Dryasque et cretus Amyntore Phoenix, Actoridaeque pares et missus ab Elide Phyleus.
source.text_original: Diffugiunt populi nec se nisi moenibus urbis / esse putant tutos, donec Meleagros et una / lecta manus iuvenum coiere cupidine laudis: / Tyndaridae gemini, spectatus caestibus alter, / alter equo, primaeque ratis molitor Iason, / et cum Pirithoo, felix concordia, Theseus; / et duo Thestiadae prolesque Aphareia, Lynceus / et velox Idas, et iam non femina Caeneus / Leucippusque ferox iaculoque insignis Acastus / Hippothousque Dryasque et cretus Amyntore Phoenix, / Actoridaeque pares et missus ab Elide Phyleus.
source.text_english: The people scatter, and they think themselves safe only within the walls of the city, until Meleager and with him a chosen band of young men gathered together, driven by a desire for glory: the twin sons of Tyndareus, one renowned for boxing gloves, the other for the horse; Jason, the builder of the first ship; Theseus, with Pirithous, in happy concord; and the two sons of Thestius and the offspring of Aphareus, Lynceus and swift Idas; and Caeneus, no longer a woman; Leucippus; fierce Acastus, distinguished for the javelin; Hippothous and Dryas; Phoenix, born of Amyntor; the equal sons of Actor; and Phyleus, sent from Elis.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Ecce per obliqui rapidum compendia montis ductor avens laetusque dolis agnoscit Acastum horrentem iaculis et parmae luce coruscum.
reuse.text_original: Ecce per obliqui rapidum compendia montis / ductor avens laetusque dolis agnoscit Acastum / horrentem iaculis et parmae luce coruscum.
reuse.text_english: Look, by the steep shortcuts of the slanting mountain, the leader, eager and glad at the stratagem, recognizes Acastus, bristling with spears and flashing with the sheen of his round shield.
